memory_verse.label: Bible Portion
memory_verse.text: "On the third day, Joseph said to them, 'Do this and you will live, for I fear God: If you are honest men, let one of your brothers stay here in prison, while the rest of you go and take grain back for your starving households. But you must bring your youngest brother to me, so that your words may be verified and that you may not die.' This they proceeded to do" - Gen 42:18-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the third day, Joseph softens his terms. Instead of keeping most of them imprisoned, he will hold only one and let the rest carry grain home to their starving families. And he gives the reason for his more merciful dealing: "for I fear God." Joseph, though he holds absolute power over these men, will not abuse it, because he answers to a higher authority — the God he reverences.

What a beautiful phrase from the ruler of Egypt: "for I fear God." The fear of God is not terror that cowers, but a deep reverence that shapes how we live and how we treat others. Because Joseph feared God, he tempered his power with mercy. He remembered that he himself was accountable to the Lord, and that others were made in God's image.

This is a mark of true godliness, especially in those who hold power. Anyone with authority — a boss, a parent, a leader, an official — is tempted to use it for their own ends. But the person who fears God handles power with restraint, fairness, and compassion, because they know they will answer to Him.

However much or little authority you have, let the fear of God shape how you use it. Do you treat those under you, or those who depend on you, with the mercy and fairness of one who knows God is watching? "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom" (Prov 9:10) — and it makes us gentler, fairer, and kinder people.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Does the fear of God shape how you treat those with less power than you?
Where might you be tempted to use authority for your own ends?
How would reverence for God change the way you use your influence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, let a healthy fear of You shape all I do. Where I have authority or influence, help me to use it with mercy and fairness, remembering that I answer to You. Amen.
